question: What is the difference between Cosine Distance, Euclidean ($L2$) Distance, and Dot Product? What is the difference between Cosine Distance, Euclidean ($L2$) Distance, and Dot Product?

options.text: Cosine measures angle regardless of magnitude; Euclidean measures geometric distance; Dot product combines angle and magnitude.
Cosine measures geometric distance between two points; Euclidean measures angle regardless of magnitude; Dot product only works for normalized vectors.
Euclidean and Dot Product are mathematically identical for all vectors; Cosine is simply Euclidean distance divided by a constant.
Dot product always produces a value between -1 and 1 like cosine similarity, so the two are interchangeable regardless of vector magnitude.

explanation: Specification answer: Cosine measures angle regardless of magnitude; Euclidean measures geometric distance; Dot product combines angle and magnitude.

question: How does the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graph index work? How does the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graph index work?

options.text: It organizes vectors into multi-layer skip-list graphs; upper layers perform long-distance routing; bottom layers perform fine-grained local search.
It organizes vectors into a single flat graph with no layers, where every node has an edge to every other node within a fixed radius, and search is simply a radius query.
It builds a strict binary tree over the vector space, similar to a k-d tree, where each level halves the search space along a different dimension.
It clusters vectors into a fixed number of centroids using k-means, and search only ever compares the query to the nearest centroid, never visiting individual vectors directly.

explanation: Specification answer: It organizes vectors into multi-layer skip-list graphs; upper layers perform long-distance routing; bottom layers perform fine-grained local search.

question: What is Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search vs Flat (Exact) k-NN? What is Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search vs Flat (Exact) k-NN?

options.text: Flat compares query against every vector ($O(N)$); ANN traverses graph or clusters in sub-linear time ($O(\log N)$) with slight recall trade-off.
Flat search uses an approximate hash-based shortcut to skip most vectors, while ANN always performs an exact O(N) comparison to guarantee correctness.
ANN and Flat search have identical time complexity; the only difference is that ANN additionally stores vectors compressed on disk.
Flat search is sub-linear because it pre-sorts vectors by magnitude, while ANN is O(N) because it must still visit every graph node before returning results.

explanation: Specification answer: Flat compares query against every vector ($O(N)$); ANN traverses graph or clusters in sub-linear time ($O(\log N)$) with slight recall trade-off.

question: What does the efsearch parameter control in HNSW graph traversal? What does the efsearch parameter control in HNSW graph traversal?

options.text: The size of the dynamic priority queue during search: higher efsearch yields higher accuracy (recall) at the cost of latency.
The maximum number of layers the HNSW graph is allowed to build at index-construction time, fixed once and never adjustable per query.
The number of vectors returned to the client per query, independent of how many candidates are examined internally during the graph traversal.
A compression ratio applied to stored vectors at query time, trading precision of each vector's components for faster distance computation.

explanation: Specification answer: The size of the dynamic priority queue during search: higher efsearch yields higher accuracy (recall) at the cost of latency.

question:
During triage in AI Vector Databases pgvector Qdrant, an engineer observes:
"System fault during operation: Vector Search Returns Irrelevant Nearest Neighbors Due to Dot Product on Unnormalized Vectors".
What is the verified root cause?

options.text: Embeddings inserted with arbitrary magnitudes while index was configured for Dot Product, causing vectors with huge norms to dominate similarity scores regardless of direction.

The index was correctly configured for Cosine distance, but the embedding model was retrained with a different dimensionality, so the stored vectors and query vectors are being compared across incompatible vector spaces.

HNSW's efSearch parameter was set too low, so the graph traversal terminates before reaching the true nearest neighbors, returning only nearby-but-suboptimal candidates regardless of the distance metric used.

The embeddings are correctly normalized to unit length, but a stale HNSW index built before the last re-embedding still references the old, unnormalized vectors, so search compares new queries against outdated candidates.

explanation:
Root Cause: Embeddings inserted with arbitrary magnitudes while index was configured for Dot Product, causing vectors with huge norms to dominate similarity scores regardless of direction.

Fix Resolution:
Normalize all vector embeddings to unit length ($L2$ norm = 1.0) before insertion: v = v / np.linalg.norm(v).
